question.text: For every real number $x \neq-1$, let $f(x)=\frac{x}{x+1}$. Write $f_1(x)=f(x)$ \& for $n \geq 2, f_n(x)=f\left(f_{n-1}(x)\right)$. Then $f_1(-2) . f_2(-2)$ $\qquad$ must be

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Hint: } f(x)=\frac{x}{x+1}, \quad f_2(x)=\frac{x}{\frac{x+1}{\frac{x}{x+1}+1}}=\frac{x}{2 x+1} \\ & f_3(x)=\frac{x}{3 x+1}, \Rightarrow f_1(-2) \cdot f_2(-2) \ldots \ldots \ldots . f_n(-2) \\ & =\frac{-2}{-1} \times \frac{-2}{-3} \times \frac{-2}{-5} \times \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots \times \frac{-2}{(2 n-1)}=\frac{2^n}{1.3 .5 \ldots .(2 n-1)}\end{aligned}$
